clue.text: Farewell that makes good past worker upset?

definitions.text: Farewell that makes good past worker upset?

parts.words: Farewell that makes good past worker upset?
parts.note: a big payment on leaving makes amends to a departing employee who may be upset at going, and it arrives with a parting clasp of hands

explanation.surface: A send-off meant to soothe a long-serving employee who is unhappy about leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes good' reads as improving the worker but means compensating them; the hint of a handshake as a farewell gesture points to the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a generous severance payment given to an employee on departure, a well-paid farewell.

clue.text: One with US military service, fine East African native

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a British armed service
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An East African who served in American and British forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East' attaches to 'African' in the surface but only gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an animal found wild only in Africa, a native of that continent.

clue.text: Left university with tot to raise — one's usually found in bed

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, so nip is read backwards

parts.note: a nip is a small drink, as is a tot

explanation.surface: Someone leaves college with a small child to bring up, who usually sleeps in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests sleep, but it is a flower bed; 'tot' is a dram, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower commonly planted in flower beds.

clue.text: Labour opponents knock back housing article

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit as opponents

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the eating word takes in the article

parts.note: to knock back food or drink is to devour it
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Political opponents of the Labour Party reject a piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to strive or work hard, the verbal sense of labour.

clue.text: Telegraph supports farm food being wild

indicators.note: in a down clue what supports another word sits under it

parts.note: hay is fodder for livestock
to wire a message is to telegraph it

explanation.surface: The Telegraph newspaper backs farm produce running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the newspaper but is the verb meaning wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Haywire is informal for out of control, erratic, the sense of wild.

clue.text: Puts in order that's consumed in empty Nando's

indicators.note: in places the consumed word inside the emptied restaurant name
an emptied word keeps only its outside letters, the first and last of Nando's

parts.note: something consumed has been eaten

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up after the food is eaten in a deserted branch of Nando's, a chicken restaurant chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatens means tidies, arranging things properly.

clue.text: Row northwards, river dwellers — but river goes west

indicators.note: to go west is to die or vanish, so the river's letter is removed
in a down clue going northwards means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: otters live in rivers

explanation.surface: Rowing up a river past otters, until the river turns west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here: a quarrel, not rowing; 'goes west' is not a direction but disappearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or argument, a row.

clue.text: Hesitate to get agitated about fine

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up, so hesitate is rearranged

parts.note: C, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: Pausing nervously over whether something is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic can mean tasteful or artistic, as in fine art, a fine-looking design.

clue.text: Guaranteed right to enter petition in extremity

indicators.note: in places the combined word inside the extremity

parts.note: an end is an extremity

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so the right letter goes inside the petition word

parts.note: to sue for something is to petition for it

explanation.surface: Someone made sure of their right to lodge a petition in dire circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ensured something is to have made certain of it, guaranteed it.

clue.text: Hammer slowly or fast

parts.note: to hammer on a door is to rap on it
doing something idly is doing it slowly and lazily

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to strike something either at a leisurely pace or at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slowly' looks like the opposite of the answer but only supplies a piece; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly and fast are both adverbs meaning at great speed, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: They sketch, maybe, putting Queen in at first with son

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places the queen's letter between the letters of at
in shows the queen's letter goes inside the word at

parts.note: R, from Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen
1ST is the written short form of first

explanation.surface: A setup describing people drawing, with a royal placed somewhere along with a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is not a selection signal here; it is written as 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching is one thing artists do, so 'maybe' marks the definition as an example of their work.

clue.text: Dream of cooler siesta, frolicking

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you

indicators.note: frolicking suggests leaping about playfully, so the word siesta has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a refreshing afternoon nap while playing about.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise about something is to daydream or imagine it longingly, the sense of 'dream of'.

clue.text: Second nag is a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter has no start, so the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to nag someone is to bother them

explanation.surface: A racehorse in second place is a nag that never really got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' and 'nag' suggest horse racing, but 'Second' is the definition and 'nag' means pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Second can mean the other one of two, as in 'every second day' or 'the other day'; both pick out an alternative.

clue.text: Peer with gong where personal decoration should hang

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A nobleman wearing a medal, with a remark about where that honour should be displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'decoration' looks like the medal, but it is an earring, which hangs from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earrings, a personal adornment, are worn hanging from the soft lower part of the ear.

clue.text: Perfect example of rock Sixties youth'll broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so what we hear is the clue's phrase

parts.note: rock is roll, and a mod was a 1960s British youth subculture member; 'roll mod'll' said aloud gives the answer

explanation.surface: A 1960s youngster will put out rock music as a shining example.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were scooter-riding 1960s British youths; 'roll' for rock, plus 'mod'll', is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person held up as an ideal example to imitate.

clue.text: Cook tasted sampling whiskey and battered flies?

indicators.note: sampling is taking in, so the reworked letters take in the extra letter
to cook the books is to rearrange them, so the letters of tasted are reworked

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cook tries some whiskey and a battered dish, perhaps fried insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' signals an anagram of TASTED into SATTED, and 'sampling' puts W inside it. 'battered' suggests cooking batter but means struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Flies that have been hit hard with a swatter have been swatted, so the definition describes them.

clue.text: Creature making a little bear mad — I'll observe

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone vows to watch an animal that drives a bear a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Creature making' as the definition, but 'making' is only a link word between the definition and the wordplay; the answer means just 'Creature'.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Sinister group stifling publicity — one may be criminal

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the group's letters surround the others

parts.note: a cult is often a sinister sect
PR, public relations, is publicity
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shadowy organisation hushes up the press, and one of its members may be a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for an offence, which is what a criminal is.

clue.text: Church with member of flock in charge of pottery

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ram is a male sheep, one of a flock

explanation.surface: A churchgoer from the congregation runs a pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member of flock' suggests a parishioner but is a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic as an adjective describes things made of fired clay, that is pottery.

clue.text: Some elements of orchestra may be nervous, almost taking pot

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the shortened word takes the pot inside
almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: timid means nervous
a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: Some orchestra players get jittery and turn to drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests cannabis but is a cooking pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are the kettledrums, one section of an orchestra's percussion.

clue.text: Silly inflammatory stuff, admitting I'm turning Conservative

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the fuel's letters take the others inside

parts.note: coal is material that burns

indicators.note: turning means the letters of I'm are read backwards

explanation.surface: A rabble-rousing remark about switching to the Tories is called foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflammatory' suggests provocative speech, but here it means combustible.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical means funny and absurd, a synonym of silly.

clue.text: Curb criminal element that's gripping area

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the element's letters hold the area letter

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Police restrain a lawbreaker's gang member who controls a district.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain something is to hold it in check, to curb or restrain it.

clue.text: Willowy Kate Moss illustration partly printed upside-down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the letters read from bottom to top
partly says only some of the letters across these words are used

explanation.surface: A picture of the slender model Kate Moss printed the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' hides EMOSSIL across 'Kate Moss illustration'; 'printed upside-down' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means slim and supple, a synonym of willowy.

clue.text: Dance with weird graduate

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone dances with a strange university leaver.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Defence revealed in tabloid — bail oddly rejected

indicators.note: rejecting the odd letters keeps the second, fourth and so on of these words

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports the defence argument after bail is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' joins the definition to the wordplay; the even letters of 'tabloid bail' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence claiming the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Frock that gives little wear?

parts.note: read as a garment that will not last long, but really a short dress, very little clothing to wear

explanation.walkthrough: 'little wear' suggests a frock that wears out quickly; it is a very small item of wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A minidress is a very short frock, so it offers only a small amount of clothing.

clue.text: Enthusiastic in punt, but starting in the opposite direction

indicators.note: the starting letter is a compass point swapped for its opposite, west becoming east

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a wager

explanation.surface: Keen on a punt, though setting off the wrong way, as on a punting boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat river boat but is a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Paid occasional visits to sierran region of Portugal

parts.note: to pay a visit is to make one, so paid stands for made

indicators.note: occasional visits touch only every other letter of the word sierran

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes visited a mountain area of Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' does double service with 'visits': paid visits are made visits, giving MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is an island archipelago forming an autonomous region of Portugal.

clue.text: Dancing galore, taking in learner's musical 9 Across

indicators.note: taking in means the jumbled letters enclose the learner's letter
dancing letters move about, so galore is jumbled

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Lots of dancing, with a novice joining, to a quick piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 Across is RAPIDLY; the answer is the musical direction for that tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian tempo marking telling musicians to play briskly.

clue.text: Uncompromising approach that leads to things piling up

definitions.meaning: a figurative sense: a policy certain to bring conflict

definitions.text: that leads to things piling up
definitions.meaning: literally a path that will end in a crash or pile-up

explanation.definitionFit: A collision course is literally a path toward a crash and figuratively a confrontational stance.
